svg.text: SERIES 1 • CARD 05 OF 09 • DOMAIN: FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ARITHMETIC • LOGARITHMIC PROPORTIONAL TOWERS • FLUSH DATUM
LESSON GUIDE: HOW TO FIND THE LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE (LCM)
Step-by-Step Hands-On Tutorial: Finding LCM(12, 18) = 36 & The Law of Conservation of Primes
Grades 4–9 Math & Pre-Algebra • Hands-On Classroom & Home STEM Studio Series

text.tspan: Decompose numbers 12 and 18 into prime building blocks:
Seat each tower in the 12-socket lid tray. Their summits
Identify the blocks they share in common (intersection):
Shared Overlap: Exactly one [2] and one [3]!
3. TAKE PRIME UNION: Take highest power of each prime: two [2]s, two [3]s.
Calculator Verification: Press Factor Tree Icon ([PRIME] / [g][FACT]) and run 12 [ENTER] 18 [GCF] 12 [ENTER] 18 [f] [LCM] → 36.

g.text: CORE PRINCIPLE: CONSERVATION OF PRIMES: A × B = GCD × LCM

text.tspan: Multiply Tower 12 and Tower 18: you have three [2]s and three [3]s. Look at your GCD Tower
([2], [3]) and your LCM Tower ([2]², [3]²): together they contain the EXACT same prime blocks!
Therefore: A × B = GCD(A, B) × LCM(A, B) = 6 × 36 = 216!
Build Tower 8: [2]+[2]+[2] and Tower 12: [2]+[2]+[3]. Prime union takes three [2]s and one [3] → LCM = 24 (28.09mm)! (Scan QR for 3D animated solution!)

g.text: → Assemble with your physical blocks, then scan the QR code to verify with the 3D step-by-step vector model.
